behaviour: A short owner answer is stored with the question it answered and judged together with it.
The reader gives each shown record its own answer from the owner's whole message instead of a relay confirming yes items.
note: Restated by SR-101, which lists SR-098 as superseded.

behaviour: Plumb gives an evidence-based assessment of how its Claude Code integration maps to Hermes.
The project-local Hermes adapter preserves instructions, reports activation conservatively and documents unsupported surfaces.
note: Release A scope may be a one-off hardening.

behaviour: A model independent of the coding agent reads the owner's message against shown records and returns accepted, rejected, change asked or open per item.
An independent judge model decides whether each new or changed record is supported by the owner's words.
On each owner message a model decides if intent starts or changes, drafts the read-back and finds blocking gaps.
Reading and judging run as batched background jobs so no hook waits on a model.
Pending owner matters come as cards with suggested resolutions, plus a summary of what was settled.
Settling starts with trial batches that calibrate on the owner's yes/no answers.
The proposed backlog is judged in one background pass and offered as per-feature trial cards.
note: Backlog migration task, not ongoing behaviour.

behaviour: Long plumb executions report the current step and progress at least once per second.
Hermes skills installed for a project are plugin-owned, safely managed and resolved only by qualified names.
Plumb selects tests for a change by the functions each test executed plus tests linked to the requirement.
Plumb reports links an edit made stale right after the edit and requires resolving them before the turn ends.
Only the owner confirms a record, via typed command, button, owner-only terminal answer or read free prose.
When a code change departs from an aligned record, plumb first checks requirement against intent before routing it.
The repin check is a model cascade where JEV clears easy links and stronger models judge the rest.
The owner turns auto-approval on or off with a typed /plumb auto-approve command the agent cannot imitate.
A card shows the record, what changed with evidence, the owner's words and each option's consequences.
A proposed requirement settles by context when links, tests and an independent consistency check all hold.
note: SR-134 forbids settling from tests and consistency alone; SR-135 supersedes it.

behaviour: A model cascade finds older records' source words in past transcripts and shows them on trial cards.
note: Tied to the trial and backlog work; may be transitional.

behaviour: A failed build of plumb's environment makes the launcher exit with the build's non-zero code.
/plumb resolves to the command only and every owner command also accepts /plumb:plumb.
The edit gate stays on unless a legacy install runs plumb hook, and reads the session gate under the nearest .plumb/.
The skills and /plumb command cover every outcome plumb can answer.
note: Broad coverage requirement; details may drift.

behaviour: The shipped plugin carries only runnable files, every hook has a timeout and it runs on all platforms.
Trial presses in the mod are labelled owner answers that calibration counts.
The session-start hook records which Python runs plumb first so the panel can always connect.
When the panel cannot reach plumb it writes one line naming the reason once per session.
Each requirement records its proof and evidence, and plumb names unproven requirements before a merge.
The commanded request check receives the last reply, recent owner messages and repository facts to resolve references.
Every card is either one request's read-back or one choice, and stands alone.
Records a read-back creates are confirmed by the answer to that read-back, and re-asked only as a choice when changed.
A recommendable option becomes a flippable assumption; only gaps without a supported option are asked.
An unanswered card is withdrawn when replaced or its branch merges, confirming nothing.
A trial card is the read-back of one record with source words found by meaning, with at most three open.
A proposed record becomes confirmed only by the owner or by the calibrated judge under auto-approve.
Redundant confirmation paths are removed and typed settle, undo and go are handled at the prompt hook.
The diagram pane draws an architecture-diagram skill file as SVG on desktop and as box text in the terminal.
The plugin ships the architecture-diagram skill and /diagram has the agent draw from the code into .diagram/.
The mod is demonstrated in a live session and passes plugin validation before being called done.
note: One-time proof for the diagram mod.

behaviour: A card naming a diagram file shows that diagram above its question, or the question alone if the mod is absent.
For questions about structure or flow, clarify tells the agent to draw a diagram and name it on the card.
A printed clarify card holds the topic, questions and suggested answers, not the read-back's lines.
plumb unlink removes one link, renumbers the rest and logs an unlink event.
plumb relink repoints one link to a new target with fresh pins and logs a relink event.
A conflict is answered on its card or by typed choose, never relayed by the agent.
